::: {.callout-important}
## Read this first

**Not medical advice. Educational use only.**

- This helper adds up **weekly minutes** — it does not set intensity. Pair it with the [HR helper](/tools/hr-calculator/index.html) or a symptom cap for the "how hard" question.
- **100 min/week** is what Howell 2021 actually **prescribed** (20 min × 5 d/wk). It is a documented prescription line, not a proven minimum dose.
- **160 min/week** is a **post hoc, observational** cutoff from the same paper — it discriminated symptom-free vs symptomatic adolescents at one month. It is not a second prescription target.
- **150 min/week** is from a **different paper, different outcome** (Howell & Wingerson 2024, sleep quality) — shown for reference only. Do not treat it as interchangeable with the 160-minute symptom line.
:::

## Why this exists

The installment [Twenty minutes from where?](/posts/pillar2-003-twenty-minutes-from-where/index.html) argues that session length is the wrong unit — the literature's actual signal is in the **weekly total**, not any single session's stopwatch reading. This page does the arithmetic so a family or clinician can see where their week actually lands.

**Related reading:** [Disagreement 2 — prescribed vs. observed](/posts/pillar2-003-twenty-minutes-from-where/index.html) · [Howell 2021 volume analysis, PMID 33856860](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33856860/)

::: {#fs-dose-calculator .fs-tool-wrap}

## Boundaries

| Topic | What this tool does / does not do |
|-------|-----------------------------------|
| **Intensity** | Not covered here — pair with the [HR helper](/tools/hr-calculator/index.html) or a symptom cap. |
| **100 vs 160** | Two different constructs from the same paper (prescribed line vs. post hoc observational cutoff). This tool labels them separately on purpose — see the installment's Disagreement 2. |
| **150 min/wk** | A different paper, a different outcome (sleep, not symptoms). Shown for reference, not merged with the 160-minute line. |
| **Session-length guilt** | Uneven session lengths that still hit the weekly total are not a protocol failure — see the installment's Pattern A. |
